      16                 :             : /// @brief Provides bitmask operators for enum classes
      17                 :             : ///
      18                 :             : /// !!!! ATTENTION !!!!
      19                 :             : /// These operators only work well on real bitmasks. Meaning, the elements of an enum must always be set to a power of
      20                 :             : /// two, and no value shall have the value 0.
      21                 :             : ///
      22                 :             : /// @see https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/named_req/BitmaskType
      23                 :             : ///
      24                 :             : /// @details One shall prefer `enum class` over `enum` since this avoids implicit conversions. This comes with the
      25                 :             : /// drawback that it is no longer possible to combine flags of an enum (which is a mechanism which is often used in
      26                 :             : /// POSIX related APIs).
      27                 :             : ///
      28                 :             : /// By implementing the named requirements for BitmaskType for such `enum class` types, we get the best of both worlds.
      29                 :             : ///
      30                 :             : /// This is in particular needed for the `lib/os`, since not all POSIX options are safety-certified. So we have to
      31                 :             : /// ensure that in a safety-use-case, only the certified options are chosen. Thus, our functions cannot take any
      32                 :             : /// integer, since this could lead that developers _leak_ not allowed numerical representations of flags into our
      33                 :             : /// functional abstractions. By using a specific type for flag combinations (enable_bitmask_operators) we can ensure
      34                 :             : /// that only valid flags are combined with each other.
      35                 :             :
